messages.title: It Restarted. What Did It Forget?
messages.subtitle: Shipment42 still says SHIPPED after a crash. The revision guard that protected it is gone.
messages.property: Restart must not let an event older than the already-authoritative projected revision regress Shipment42.
messages.takeaway: Correct recovery restores the evidence and protocol state needed to make the same safety decisions after restart.
messages.step.revision-44.title: Revision 44 reaches the projection
messages.step.revision-44.lead: The authoritative event sets Shipment42 to SHIPPED at revision 44. Track the business value and the decision guard separately.
messages.step.durable-value.title: The business value is durable
messages.step.durable-value.lead: The store saves SHIPPED. A restart can read that value again, but the value alone does not say which revision produced it.
messages.step.memory-guard.title: The guard lives in memory
messages.step.memory-guard.lead: The handler remembers lastAppliedRevision = 44 only in this process. It uses that number to reject older events.
messages.step.reject-before.title: Revision 42 is rejected before the crash
messages.step.reject-before.lead: The delayed PROCESSING event carries revision 42. The live guard knows 42 < 44, so SHIPPED remains.
messages.step.crash.title: The process crashes
messages.step.crash.lead: The durable value and the memory guard cross different survival boundaries. Watch which one remains.
messages.step.restart.title: A new process starts
messages.step.restart.lead: Starting a process does not make it ready to decide which event is authoritative.
messages.step.value-survives.title: SHIPPED survives
messages.step.value-survives.lead: The restarted process reads Shipment42 = SHIPPED from storage. That is a business value, not a recovered ordering guard.
messages.step.guard-disappears.title: The guard is empty
messages.step.guard-disappears.lead: lastAppliedRevision was not durable. The new process has no remembered revision for Shipment42.
messages.step.stale-arrives.title: Revision 42 arrives again
messages.step.stale-arrives.lead: The delayed PROCESSING event is the same older event the previous process rejected.
messages.step.weak-accepts.title: The weak handler regresses the value
messages.step.weak-accepts.lead: An empty guard treats revision 42 as new and writes PROCESSING. Business-data durability did not preserve the safety decision.
messages.step.property.title: Name the recovery property
messages.step.property.lead: After restart, an older event must still be rejected when a newer authoritative revision was already projected.
messages.step.atomic-record.title: Persist one coherent record
messages.step.atomic-record.lead: Store state = SHIPPED; applied_revision = 44 atomically. Two unrelated writes can leave a mismatched value and revision after a crash.
messages.step.restart-again.title: Restart with the stronger record
messages.step.restart-again.lead: This time storage contains the value and its applied revision as one authoritative point.
messages.step.recover-44.title: Recover revision 44 before readiness
messages.step.recover-44.lead: Restore both fields before accepting events or declaring the projection ready.
messages.step.reject-after.title: Revision 42 stays rejected
messages.step.reject-after.lead: The recovered guard proves 42 < 44. SHIPPED cannot be overwritten by PROCESSING.
messages.step.accept-45.title: Revision 45 is a positive control
messages.step.accept-45.lead: The recovered guard must still allow a genuinely newer event. Revision 45 advances state and revision together.
messages.step.cache-control.title: A rebuildable cache is different
messages.step.cache-control.lead: A display cache derived from the authoritative record may be discarded and rebuilt. It does not make the ordering decision.
messages.step.replay-alternative.title: Replay can rebuild the guard
messages.step.replay-alternative.lead: A complete authoritative history can reconstruct value and revision before readiness, if replayed effects are safe to repeat.
messages.step.checkpoint-mismatch.title: A checkpoint can disagree with state
messages.step.checkpoint-mismatch.lead: A revision-44 snapshot with a revision-43 checkpoint describes different logical points. Replaying from 43 needs a repeat-safe contract.
messages.step.schema-compatibility.title: One more recovery question
messages.step.schema-compatibility.lead: The recovered revision resolves this counterexample. A new software version raises another question; explore it in Deep Dive.
messages.step.remaining.title: What can still go wrong?
messages.step.remaining.lead: An incomplete replay source, mismatched recovery artifacts, incompatible data, or external effects can still break recovery.
messages.step.transfer.title: Transfer: the payment importer
messages.step.transfer.lead: Account state is durable through offset 500, but a memory-only checkpoint resets to zero. What must hold before replay is safe?
messages.step.recap.title: Ask the Six Questions
messages.step.recap.lead: Follow the evidence, authority, and survival boundary before calling a restarted process ready.
messages.visual.title: Before / After Restart
messages.rail.evidenceBefore: Revision 44 is authoritative; the live guard rejects revision 42.
messages.rail.evidenceLost: After restart, SHIPPED survives but the guard is empty.
messages.rail.evidenceRegression: Revision 42 is accepted and regresses Shipment42 to PROCESSING.
messages.rail.evidenceRecovered: A coherent record restores SHIPPED and revision 44 before readiness.
messages.rail.evidenceControl: Recovered revision 44 rejects 42 and accepts 45; a cache may be rebuilt.
messages.rail.contractWeak: Persisting only the business value leaves the ordering decision unprotected.
messages.rail.contractStrong: Persist or safely reconstruct state and applied revision as one coherent authority point before serving events.
messages.rail.contractScope: Only correctness state needed for the decision must survive or be rebuilt; disposable caches may reset.
messages.rail.propertyHidden: Which safety decision must remain possible after restart?
messages.rail.property: An older event cannot regress the already-authoritative projected revision after restart.
messages.challenge.title: What evidence rejects revision 42?
messages.challenge.intro: After restart, storage says SHIPPED, memory guard is empty, and revision 42 / PROCESSING arrives.
messages.challenge.question: Under the weak design, what can the restarted process use to prove revision 42 is stale?
messages.option.recoveredRevision: Nothing; the revision was not recovered
messages.challenge.feedback: The weak design has no revision evidence. Recover a coherent applied revision, or rebuild it from authoritative history before readiness.
messages.deepDive.title: What does correct recovery require?
messages.deepDive.section1.title: Business value versus correctness state
messages.deepDive.section1.body: SHIPPED survived, but the revision used to reject older events did not. A readable value is not proof that the handler can make the same safety decision after restart.
messages.deepDive.section2.title: Atomicity and readiness
messages.deepDive.section2.body: State and applied revision must describe one coherent point. Do not accept events while restoring only one field, or declare the process ready simply because it started.
messages.deepDive.section3.title: Replay and checkpoints
messages.deepDive.section3.body: Complete authoritative replay can rebuild both fields before readiness. A snapshot at revision 44 and checkpoint at 43 need a repeat-safe replay contract; neither artifact alone proves coherence.
messages.deepDive.section4.title: Durable format compatibility
messages.deepDive.section4.body: A new binary may misread old durable bytes. Validate or migrate schema before recovered state becomes authoritative. External effects may need their own recovery protocol.
messages.deepDive.section5.title: Across eight boundaries
messages.deepDive.section5.body: Logical operation identity, processed-event evidence, and authority state can each be lost at a different boundary. The series asks what evidence must survive for every decision, rather than persisting every variable.
messages.recap.1: Evidence: what proves the previously applied revision?
messages.recap.2: Authority: which record or history is authoritative after restart?
messages.recap.3: Durability: which value and correctness metadata survived together?
messages.recap.4: Delivery: what may replay, and can its effect repeat safely?
messages.recap.5: Ordering: which revision supersedes this incoming event?
messages.recap.6: Recovery: what must be restored before readiness?
